text:
jin (oncall): FYI: rolling maintenance planned across apac1 + euc2 for ephemeral-disk cleanup + kernel micropatch. Start: 2026-06-02T02:00:00Z, end window 06:00Z. Expected impact: brief node drains, ~10-14% GPU capacity reduced in apac1 at any one time. Will do staggered node operations to avoid pool starvation.

alex (infra): tagging in the capacity table — we should keep 2 spare nodes per pool (gpu-pool-a/gpu-pool-b) during the window. I increased backfill budget on the scheduler to 30% for the window.

ben (sre): what is the largest expected disruption per node? how long is each drain+cleanup?

jin (oncall): per-node drain ~12-25 minutes depending on eviction pacing and disk scrub (older VMs). Typical: 5m drain (grace periods + pod eviction), 7-15m disk cleanup/kernel apply, 3m kubelet restart and healthcheck. Worst-case 30m. We'll do 10m gaps between node starts to avoid thundering herd.

carla (eng-runtime): please ensure model-serving routes have a fallback. Recommend routing low-priority hosted traffic to eu-cold cluster or to dedicated-pool when apac capacity drops >8%. We can add a temporary routing policy: route_by_policy("latency<=120ms,region=apac1") fallback -> euc2.

sam (ops-scheduler): calendar invite created + maint-bot scheduled notifications. maint-bot will post 30m/10m/1m before each az wave.

maint-bot: Scheduled maintenance: apac1 wave 1 nodes n1-n6 02:00Z-02:40Z, wave 2 n7-n12 02:40Z-03:20Z. euc2 planned 03:30Z-04:30Z.

alex (infra): drain command for reference (we'll use graceful eviction + local-ssd-prep):

```bash
kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120 --force
# then ssh -> sudo nvme secure-erase /dev/nvme0n1 (if needed) && sudo reboot
```

ben (sre): add a preflight check for any nodes with >90% disk usage; skip auto-erase if disk health is poor. We should also flag nodes with older kernel versions (<=5.10) for manual follow-up.

jin (oncall): agreed. Preflight job will produce a CSV: node, disk% , kernel, replicate_count. I'll attach in thread. If replicate_count < 2 we'll hold that node until manual approval.

carla (eng-runtime): one more ask: can we mute health alerts for model-availability on routes that are intentionally routed away? Otherwise we'll spam pager rotation.

sam (ops-scheduler): will update alert routing: create temporary suppression rule for alert "model-serving-degraded" tagged with region:apac1 during window.

alex (infra): capacity numbers: apac1 current GPU pool = 240 GPUs across pools, with 12 nodes scheduled -> expected 28 GPUs offline per wave (~11.7%). We'll monitor queue lengths; if queued tokens > 150k for >5m, switch fast-fail policy to reduce tail latency.

ben (sre): any cost implications for backfilling from eu->apac cross-region? egress + inter-region charges. Estimate: ~0.6 cpm extra for heavy reroute. Ops, confirm cost center.

sam (ops-scheduler): cost noted and assigned to ENG-OPS budget line for the maintenance.

jin (oncall): quick checklist before wave 1:
- preflight CSV ok
- backfill budget set to 30%
- suppression rule in place
- fallback route enabled
- oncall pager assigned (ben/jin)

alex (infra): I'll start wave 1 at 02:03Z if preflight green. Will ping here when node1 drained.

maint-bot: wave1-started n1 at 02:03:14Z.

ben (sre): saw n1 drain, pods gracefully evicted, no rollout failures.

carla (eng-runtime): saw a small bump in p95 (20ms -> 35ms) for a minute, then normalized. :thumbsup:

jin (oncall): good call. continuing waves. I'll post postmortem if anything >30m or >10% drop sustained.

sam (ops-scheduler): leaving this thread open for post-maint notes.

alex (infra): noted — will upload node logs to /mnt/maintenance-logs/2168004321 once all waves complete.

maint-bot: maintenance-complete summary: apac1 wave1..2 success, euc2 success, total downtime per node avg 18m, no escalations.
